name: ZOI
address: Obala hrvatskog narodnog preporoda 23, Split (Riva); Gault&Millau gives no. 3
tier: THE BERTHS · THE GRAND TABLES — THE RIVA, A COUNTER BY THE HARBOUR, AND THE SEA AT FIRULE
recognition: Gault&Millau Croatia 2026: 17/20, Prestige Restaurant; listed in the MICHELIN Guide Croatia (selected, no star)
what_to_order: Tasting menu|Raw tuna, smoked to order|Brač lamb
reservation: Essential; book directly with the restaurant
notes: The tasting menu on the top-floor terrace
verdict: The most complete grand dinner in the city centre, and the one Gault&Millau ranks highest of these three at 17/20. You pay for the terrace as much as the plates, and the price sits in MICHELIN's top bracket. Book the terrace, take the tasting menu, and confirm it is trading before you promise it to guests in November.
caveat: Dinner only; winter schedule not published, call before promising it after October; online booking not via MICHELIN

name: Krug
tier: THE GRAND TABLES — THE RIVA, A COUNTER BY THE HARBOUR, AND THE SEA AT FIRULE
recognition: One MICHELIN star (2025 guide; 2026 not re-confirmed here) · Gault&Millau 16.5/20 (2026)
price_range: Tasting menus only (price not re-seen, Oct 2026)
notes: The nine-course menu at the counter.
verdict: The most ambitious cooking in the city, and the most intimate room: a counter, a short and a long menu, and the chef in front of you. Whether the star was kept in the 2026 guide we could not confirm from here; the Gault&Millau 2026 review is current. Book well ahead: there are only about twelve seats.
caveat: About twelve seats: book well ahead; hours and the 2026–27 winter schedule not published in what we found, so call.

name: Dvor
tier: THE GRAND TABLES — THE RIVA, A COUNTER BY THE HARBOUR, AND THE SEA AT FIRULE
recognition: Gault&Millau Croatia 2026: 16/20, Remarkable Restaurant; has a MICHELIN Guide page (€€€€), 2026 selection status not dated in extracts
what_to_order: Ceviche of fish, scampi and scallops|Prawn carpaccio|Grilled whole fish|Rack of lamb|Brodet
reservation: Recommended; ask for the sea-view terrace
notes: The fish, scampi and scallop ceviche in citrus emulsion, at sunset
verdict: The sea-terrace night of the three, and the quieter one: you leave the old town behind and eat facing the open water. MICHELIN puts it in its top price bracket, and Gault&Millau ranks it just behind ZOI. It has historically taken a winter break, so it belongs to an October evening, not a December one, unless the house confirms otherwise.
caveat: Historically closes for a winter break and reopens late Feb or early March; 2026-27 dates not found, call ahead

name: Konoba Fetivi
tier: VELI VAROŠ — THE KONOBAS OF THE FISHERMEN'S QUARTER
recognition: Selected in the MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2026 (no star, no Bib); Gault&Millau Croatia 2026 13/20; Falstaff 2026 85 points
what_to_order: Crni rižot|Fish of the day, grilled|Pasta with shrimp|Tuna steak|Squid stew|Gregada
notes: Black cuttlefish risotto, then a fish chosen from the plate
verdict: The one Varoš konoba with both MICHELIN and Gault&Millau behind it in 2026, and still priced like a neighbourhood room. Choose the fish from the plate, take the black risotto, drink the house white. It is small and popular, so book; and confirm the closing day, because the listings disagree.
caveat: Book ahead; closing day disputed (Sunday or Monday), call first

name: Konoba Matejuška
tier: VELI VAROŠ — THE KONOBAS OF THE FISHERMEN'S QUARTER
recognition: Family-run fish grill by the Matejuška harbour; no MICHELIN or Gault&Millau 2026 listing found
what_to_order: Marinated tuna|Grilled fish by weight|Crni rižot|House wine
reservation: Advised in summer; go for 19:30 or 21:30
notes: Tuna marinated in red wine and herbs, then grilled fish by weight
verdict: An honest fisherman's grill rather than a destination, and useful for exactly that: a late, simple fish dinner close to the harbour. We found nothing dated 2026, so treat it as likely but unconfirmed, and call before sending guests. Bring cash.
caveat: No 2026 evidence found; cash preferred; small terrace fills early

name: Šperun Eat and Drink
tier: VELI VAROŠ — THE KONOBAS OF THE FISHERMEN'S QUARTER
recognition: Casual Varoš konoba; Tripadvisor 4.0 from about 950 reviews; no MICHELIN or Gault&Millau listing found
notes: Grilled sardines with a glass of local white
verdict: A dependable, unpretentious table for a casual night, not a culinary event: ratings are solid rather than high, and one June 2026 reviewer found the pasta heavy. Stick to the grill, take the terrace, and use it when the better-known Varoš houses are full.
caveat: Book the terrace in July-August; hours conflict, call ahead

name: Apetit
address: Šubićeva 5, Split (Split Curated gives Ulica Pavla Šubića 2)
tier: IN AND AROUND THE PALACE WALLS
recognition: Upper-floor dining room in the 15th-century Papalić Palace; no MICHELIN or Gault&Millau 2026 listing found
verdict: A calm, mid-to-upper-priced lunch inside the palace quarter, good when guests want the old dishes without the street noise. Reviews are mixed on consistency and service, and no guide rates it in 2026, so take it for the room and the pašticada rather than for ambition.
caveat: Upper floor, stairs only (floor disputed); no guide rating in 2026
hot_this_month: Dalmatian pašticada, a winter dish, on a quiet first floor away from the cruise-day crowds (checked 23 Oct 2026).

name: Villa Spiza
tier: THE BERTHS · IN AND AROUND THE PALACE WALLS
recognition: Walk-in counter kitchen inside the palace; Gault&Millau Croatia 2026 entry (Popular, no score shown in extracts); Falstaff 84 points (2025)
what_to_order: Grilled fish|Crni rižot|Homemade pasta with seafood or mushrooms|Artichokes|Chocolate cake
notes: Whatever fish is on the board, then Nada's chocolate cake
verdict: The best-value plate inside the walls and the one with a queue to prove it: in summer the wait can reach two hours. Come early, bring cash, accept what is on the board. In late autumn the line shortens, but the hours shrink too, so check its social pages on the day.
caveat: No reservations, cash only; winter hours shorter and closed Sundays

name: Bokeria Kitchen & Wine
tier: IN AND AROUND THE PALACE WALLS
recognition: Gault&Millau Croatia 2026: 13.5/20 (same in 2025); not found in the MICHELIN Guide
what_to_order: Octopus|Risotto|Carpaccio|Sea bass|Fish tacos|Croatian wine by the glass
notes: Octopus, with a Croatian bottle chosen from the walls
verdict: A reliable, well-run modern bistro with a serious Croatian wine list, more useful for its hours and its bottles than for any single plate. Reviewers find the presentation stronger than some of the flavours, and prices sit above the Split average. Book, especially for dinner.
caveat: Reserve even off-season; prices above the local average

name: Zinfandel Food & Wine Bistro
tier: THE NEW SPLIT BISTROS — THE WINE LIST FIRST
recognition: Selected in the MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2026 (modern cuisine, €€); distinction category not shown in extracts
what_to_order: Pasta with prošek sauce and prawns|Sharing board|Croatian wines by the glass
notes: Pasta with prošek sauce and prawns, with a glass of Tribidrag or Plavac Mali
verdict: The most useful glass in the old town now that Paradox is reported closed, and the only wine bar in this guide with a MICHELIN listing in 2026. The food is better than bar snacks, the room is busy and close. Go for a flight of Croatian reds before or after dinner, or make it the dinner itself. Hours vary by source, so call.
caveat: Hours conflict across sources (some say closed Sunday, some Monday); small room, book at night
hot_this_month: The bar built around Tribidrag, Zinfandel's Croatian name: the glass to order in the week of Martinje, 11 November (checked 23 Oct 2026).

name: Šug
tier: THE NEW SPLIT BISTROS — THE WINE LIST FIRST
recognition: Gault&Millau Croatia 2026: 13.5/20, Chef's Restaurant; has a MICHELIN Guide page (2026 status not dated in extracts; not a 2026 Bib Gourmand)
what_to_order: Tećade|Fresh fish of the day|Pašticada with gnocchi|Skradinski rižot|Crni rižot|Grilled Adriatic tuna
price_range: MICHELIN €€€ (seen Oct 2026); Gault&Millau calls prices reasonable
notes: A teća of the day, the slow-braised pot dish
verdict: Not a grand table: a small, well-priced house that cooks the Dalmatian repertoire properly, which is rarer in the centre than it should be. Good for a guest who wants pašticada or a rižot without the tourist-menu version. Reservations are mandatory and the room is small, so it fits a last-minute dinner only if you call early.
caveat: Reservation mandatory; small room; hours conflict across listings, call ahead

name: Konoba Marjan
tier: WHERE THE CITY EATS — A FAMILY KONOBA AND THE ĆEVAPI
recognition: Family-run fish konoba; Tripadvisor 4.5 from about 2,100 reviews, 2025 Travellers' Choice
what_to_order: Cuttlefish brujet|Gregada|Black risotto|Prawn pasta|Grilled fish of the day
notes: Whole grilled fish of the day, or cuttlefish brujet
verdict: A real fish konoba rather than a palace-front trap, and well loved for its grill. It is small, so it fills and the kitchen runs out: one spring 2026 diner found the black risotto gone by 7:30 pm, and others reported slow service on full nights. Book, come early, and order the fish of the day rather than the menu standards.
caveat: Very few tables: book; dishes sell out by mid-evening; hours differ across listings

name: Kantun Paulina
tier: WHERE THE CITY EATS — A FAMILY KONOBA AND THE ĆEVAPI
recognition: Long-running takeaway ćevapi window, opening year disputed (1967 / 1979)
price_range: Small EUR 6.50, medium 8.50, large 10.50 (Tripadvisor review, Oct 2025; not re-seen in 2026)
notes: A medium portion of ćevapi in lepinja with ajvar and onion
verdict: The quick meal that locals argue about rather than a sit-down, and good value next to anything on the Riva. Reviews in 2025 still put it among the best ćevapi in town, with a few saying it has slipped. Expect a line, bring cash, eat standing or on the move.
caveat: Cash only; queues; few seats; no 2026-dated evidence found

name: Pazar (Green Market)
address: Stalls along the east wall of Diocletian's Palace by the Silver Gate (Srebrna vrata), Split
tier: LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE FISHERMEN'S BUFFET
recognition: Split's main open-air green market, daily, by the palace east wall
what_to_order: Dried figs (suhe smokve)|Paški sir|Seasonal tomatoes and greens|Dalmatian olive oil
price_range: Produce about EUR 1–6 per kg; cheese about EUR 5–35 per kg (undated guide; not re-seen in Oct 2026)
notes: Dried figs, Pag cheese and a bottle of local olive oil for the boat
verdict: The place to provision a galley and to see what is in season before choosing a konoba. Go early, carry cash and taste before you buy; the second ring of stalls sells souvenirs and imported fruit. Not a place to eat, but the most honest view of the Dalmatian table in town.
caveat: Go before 9:00; stalls thin out by noon; cash
hot_this_month: The new olive oil from Brač and Šolta starts to reach the stalls with the harvest; go at 08:00 for the producers, and note the holidays of 1 and 18 November (checked 23 Oct 2026).

name: Ribarnica (Fish Market)
address: Kraj Sv. Marije, off Marmontova, Split
tier: LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE FISHERMEN'S BUFFET
recognition: Split's morning fish market, year-round, cash
notes: Whole line-caught fish, bought by weight for the galley
verdict: Go before the konoba lunch to learn what is in season and what it costs before you see it on a menu. Buyers for galleys can deal here directly, in cash. The best whole fish go before 9:00. Do not come after 13:00, and check Sunday before you plan around it.
caveat: Cash; best fish go before 9:00; Sunday opening disputed
hot_this_month: Autumn fish: cuttlefish, squid, grouper and sea bream; arrive early, as the market closes around 13:00 (checked 23 Oct 2026).

name: Buffet Fife
tier: THE BERTHS · LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE FISHERMEN'S BUFFET
recognition: Long-running Split canteen on Matejuška; Tripadvisor reviews dated July–September 2026
what_to_order: Pašticada with njoki|Fish soup|Fried squid (lignje)|Grilled fish
price_range: About EUR 20–30 a head (blog figure, undated; not re-seen in Oct 2026)
reservation: Walk-in; bookings reportedly only for large groups
notes: Pašticada with gnocchi, or fried squid if the pašticada has run out
verdict: The honest cheap lunch on the waterfront, not a destination for cooking. Portions are big and prices low by Riva standards, and it is one of the few tables here that seems to trade through the winter. Expect queues at peak times and brisk service. Send the crew, not the guests who want a tablecloth.
caveat: Queues at peak times; reservations reportedly only for large groups; one reviewer found it cash only
hot_this_month: Pašticada with gnocchi is back in its season, the cold months, at weekday lunch by the fishing harbour (checked 23 Oct 2026).
